**May is absent in all three years.** The printed serials support that as a fact about the source set rather than merely about MIW's backlog: the 2024 serials run &hellip;2404, 2406&hellip; and the 2025 serials run &hellip;2504, 2506&hellip;, with nothing at 2405 or 2505. It is still recorded as source metadata, not as a finding about the examination calendar: MIW holds no official confirmation that no May sitting took place.

Source copies are **third-party, unverified**. No independently authoritative DG Shipping or MMD copy has been located or compared, so no paper may be described as an officially verified source. Host identity is recorded locally only, outside this public repository. The PDFs themselves are git-ignored by `.gitignore:42` and must be neither committed nor deleted.

### A note on the 2024 serial numbers

The 2025 and 2026 copies print a four-digit serial that encodes the sitting (`EM - 2509` is September 2025). Three of the 2024 copies do not: January prints `EM - 24117-1`, February `EM - 19224-1` and March `EM - 18324-1`, none of which decode to their own month. April onwards reverts to the four-digit form. The serial is recorded exactly as printed and **is not used to identify a paper**; the month printed at the head of each copy is.

## Marks

Every question is recorded at 16 marks under printed instruction 2 ("All questions carry equal marks"). Six answered questions therefore total 96 against a printed **Total Marks - 100**. The discrepancy is printed on the source copy and is reproduced, not corrected.

### Questions printing NO mark allocation

**53 of 351**, across 12 papers. Each is recorded at 16 with `printed_marks_absent` set. The omission is the printed copy's, not a transcription loss, and the corpus proves it twice over: `QP2506-Q9` prints no marks where the identical question printed (16) in August, and `QP2511-Q4` prints none where the identical question printed (16) in December.

Printed marks are **metadata, not examiner wording**. `recurrence_model.normalise_stem` removes a marks token before comparing two stems, so the same task set once with a printed (16) and once without is EXACT rather than "reworded". Three real pairs in this corpus turn on exactly that, and the guard against over-stripping is tested in `recurrence_check.py`.

| QP2604-Q6 | THE PAPER'S PRINTED ARITHMETIC IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT ON THIS QUESTION, AND THAT HAS BEEN RECORDED RATHER THAN CORRECTED. Four limbs are printed, each carrying a printed (5): a) (5), b) (5), c) (5), d) (5). Those figures sum to 20. Instruction 2 on the same paper states that all questions carry equal marks, and the paper prints a total of 100 for six answered questions, which values every question at 16. Every other question on this paper sums to exactly 16. This one does not, and no reading reconciles the two: 20 is not 16. The printed limb figures are therefore carried here as PROSE, exactly as printed, and the machine-readable subpart marks are deliberately left null - writing 5 into each would assert a 20-mark total that the paper's own instructions contradict, and normalising them to 4 would invent figures the examiner never printed. The question is recorded at the paper's equal-marks value of 16. This is a NEW anomaly for the series: the four earlier papers all carry the 96-versus-100 discrepancy at paper level, but none of them carries an internal limb-versus-question conflict on a single question. |
